title: JPEG, PNG, RAW, WebP: Which image format for the web?
h1: JPEG, PNG, RAW, WebP: Which image format for the web?
metaTitle: Web image formats: a guide for product photography
description: Discover the best image formats (JPEG, WebP, AVIF...) for product, commercial and e-commerce photography. Optimize quality, file size and SEO.
author: PackshotCreator
content:
Optimizing your images means optimizing your sales

In e-commerce and product photography, every visual detail influences the decision to buy. A product image of poor quality, too slow to load, or poorly adapted to mobile displays can scare a customer away in a split second.
The choice of image format is therefore not a secondary technical decision: it is a commercial performance lever. So, between JPEG, PNG, WebP, and the recent AVIF, which one should you choose for your product visuals? Here is a simple, accurate and business-oriented guide to help you make the right choice.

The most used image formats for the web

RAW — for capture only

‍

‍

The RAW format contains all image data captured by the camera sensor, without compression or processing. It offers maximum editing flexibility, but is never suitable for online distribution because of its large file size and its incompatibility with browsers.
Orbitvu Studios capture images in very high quality, then process them locally before automatically exporting them to formats optimized for the web.

JPEG — the effective classic

‍

‍

The JPEG format remains the most widely used on the web today. It is lightweight, widely compatible and offers a good compromise between quality and file size. However, compression should be applied in moderation to avoid image degradation.
Orbitvu studios allow you to automatically adjust the compression level according to your priority: visual quality or loading speed.

PNG — for visuals with transparency

The PNG format is ideal for visuals that require transparency (logos, cut-out images) and for keeping a sharp image thanks to its lossless compression.
Its main drawback: heavier files, which are slower to load. Orbitvu studios only export to PNG when transparency is essential.

WebP — the web format par excellence

The WebP format combines effective compression, visual quality and transparency support. It is supported by most modern browsers. For older browsers, a JPEG fallback is recommended.
Orbitvu studios handle this automatically, with a dual WebP + JPEG export if required.

AVIF — the future of visual performance

The AVIF format offers even more powerful compression than WebP, while supporting transparency and maintaining very high visual quality.
Since version 24.1.0, Orbitvu Station has offered export to the AVIF format. This format is gaining adoption and provides a strategic edge for those who want to prepare their site for future requirements in terms of performance and SEO.

faqs.question: What are the new formats supported by Orbitvu?
faqs.answer: Orbitvu Station 24.2.0 now supports exporting presentations in AVIF and WebP formats, both locally and to Orbitvu SUN Cloud. These next-generation formats allow optimal compression while maintaining image quality.

faqs.question: How does Orbitvu manage format compatibility?
faqs.answer: The Orbitvu SUN service intelligently manages image formats by using WebP when the browser supports it, and automatically switches to JPEG or PNG if necessary. This approach ensures universal compatibility.

faqs.question: What is the best image format for an e-commerce site in 2025?
faqs.answer: The WebP format is now the most recommended for an e-commerce site. It offers an excellent compromise between visual quality, reduced file size and loading speed. It also improves search engine optimization (SEO). For even better performance, the AVIF format is becoming an alternative to consider, especially if your CMS supports it.

faqs.question: Why are my product images slowing down my website?
faqs.answer: In 90% of cases, it is because they are too heavy or poorly compressed. Formats like PNG (used incorrectly) or JPEGs that are not optimized can double the loading time of a page. Thanks to Orbitvu studios, your visuals are automatically exported in the ideal format, with the right level of compression.

faqs.question: Is AVIF better than WebP?
faqs.answer: Yes, in some cases. The AVIF format offers more powerful compression than WebP, while maintaining exceptional visual quality and supporting transparency. It's ideal for high-traffic sites where every millisecond counts. Since version 24.1.0, Orbitvu supports AVIF export.
